rounds.text: Naksh Precious Metals Ltd presents a compelling case for deep-value investors due to its pristine balance sheet, as the company has successfully eliminated all borrowings, moving from Rs 5.00 Cr to Rs 0.00 Cr in just one year [E30, E44]. This conservative financial position is bolstered by the fact that capital expenditure is largely completed, with Capital Work in Progress dropping to zero, signaling that new capacity is ready to come online [E31]. Despite recent market headwinds, the stock is trading at a significant discount, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.64x, which is substantially lower than the sector benchmark of 2.87x [E1, E6, E45]. Furthermore, the company has demonstrated an ability to generate liquidity, producing Rs 0.58 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 0.75 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E25, E26]. While the company has shown a recent surge in growth with 153% compounded sales growth over the last three years, it is important to acknowledge the volatility in its operational performance [E14, E22]. Conceded: the company faces significant challenges, including a negative return on equity [E8, E11], a decline in promoter holdings [E32, E48], and a poor track record of share price growth [E17, E18].

Naksh Precious Metals Ltd exhibits severe operational deterioration, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -28% and a 5-year decline of -24% [E12, E13]. Profitability metrics are deeply concerning, with ROA, ROE, and ROCE all significantly trailing sector benchmarks at -7.22%, -6.17%, and -8.83% respectively [E7, E8, E9]. The company’s operating margin has collapsed from -6% three years ago to -41% in March 2026, while quarterly margins have also contracted by 4 percentage points year-over-year [E20, E21]. Investor confidence appears to be waning, as evidenced by a 40% decline in share price over three years and a promoter holding that has dropped from 34.03% to 24.89% [E17, E32]. The stock’s technical profile is equally weak, with a relative-strength rating of 0 against the Nifty 500 and a price currently sitting below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E36, E37]. Conceded: the company is almost debt-free with borrowings at Rs 0.00 Cr [E28, E30, E44], and it trades at a discount to book value [E1, E45]. Despite these balance sheet features, the rules-based screen assigns the company a low score of 25 out of 100, reflecting the underlying fundamental risks [E49].

The bear focuses on historical sales declines [E12, E13] while ignoring the recent 153% compounded sales growth over the last three years, which indicates a significant operational turnaround [E14]. While the bear highlights negative profitability metrics [E7, E8, E9], it overlooks the fact that the company has successfully eliminated all debt, moving from Rs 5.00 Cr in borrowings to Rs 0.00 Cr in just one year [E30, E44]. Conceded: the company has experienced a decline in promoter holding [E32, E48] and a contraction in operating margins [E20, E21]. However, the bear fails to acknowledge that the capital expenditure cycle is now complete, as evidenced by the 100% reduction in capital work in progress [E31], which positions the company to benefit from new capacity without the burden of debt. The current valuation at 0.64x book value [E1, E45] provides a substantial margin of safety that the bear dismisses by focusing solely on technical indicators like the 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E36]. Finally, the bear’s reliance on the 25/100 screen score [E49] ignores the positive cash flow generation of Rs 0.75 Cr in free cash flow [E26] and the recent quarter-over-quarter profit improvement [E50].

The bull’s reliance on 153% three-year sales growth [E14] is misleading when viewed against the long-term reality of a 28% compounded sales decline over the last decade [E12] and a 24% decline over five years [E13]. While the company is debt-free [E30, E44], this does not compensate for the fact that the business is fundamentally destroying value, evidenced by a negative ROE of -6.1% [E11] and an ROA of -7.22% [E7]. Conceded: the company has eliminated debt [E30] and completed its capital expenditure cycle [E31]. However, this "new capacity" has failed to translate into profitability, as operating margins have collapsed by 35 percentage points over three years [E20] and further contracted by 4 percentage points in the most recent quarter [E21]. The bull cites a 0.64x book value as a margin of safety [E1, E45], but this ignores the market’s assessment of the company’s terminal decline, reflected in a 43% annual price drop [E38] and a relative-strength rating of zero [E37]. Finally, the bull’s focus on positive free cash flow [E26] ignores that the company’s operating cash flow is -105% of its operating profit [E27], and the declining promoter stake [E32, E48] suggests that those closest to the business are losing confidence.
